subject: Sev1: reserved-capacity depletion threatens Payfolio throughput — immediate avoidance plan
messages:
From: Alex Chen <ops@payfolio.com>
To: dylan_brooks
Cc: marissa_cole
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — urgent

Dylan / Marissa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and end-to-end latency from our Redwood Dedicated instance starting ~08:45 PST. Token throughput for our reserved capacity has fallen to ~40% of the expected baseline and queueing is piling up (spikes in queue depth and request timeouts). This is impacting checkout flows for ~12% of live transactions.

Quick facts from our side:
- Error spike began: 2026-11-21T08:45:00Z
- Observed 5xx rate: 4.2% (baseline ~0.1%)
- Median response time: 1.8s -> 6.4s
- Prefix cache hit ratio fell 35% in the window

We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for a reliable short-term workaround (failover, routing to hosted pool, or burst authorization). Can you confirm we won't be running into token/data residency issues if we route to hosted fallback?

Attaching a small set of screenshots/metrics for the last 60 minutes. Please advise an on-call bridge if that's the right next step.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Site Reliability, Payfolio
ops@payfolio.com

Attachment(s): metrics-20261121-ops.png
From: dylan_brooks
To: Alex Chen <ops@payfolio.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, jonas_weber
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — urgent

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. We see the same signal from our side (alerting hit at 08:46 PST). I'm spinning up an incident bridge now and have asked infra to evaluate two immediate mitigations: (1) route a subset of Payfolio traffic to a hosted fallback pool in us-west-2 while preserving the reserved allocation, and (2) temporarily authorize burst GPUs to relieve the dedicated pool.

Quick asks from us to you:
- Can Payfolio tolerate routing a small percentage (~10-20%) of user requests to a hosted fallback for up to 4 hours?
- Any regulatory constraints we need to be aware of for that routing?

I've CC'd Jonas to pull procurement & exec-level approval if we need emergency burst capacity (we'll need a short authorization). Bridge details in 2 minutes.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole
To: jonas_weber, vivek_kulkarni, rishi_malhotra
Cc: dylan_brooks
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — internal summary + recommended immediate actions

Team — internal triage notes (short):
1) Root signal: sudden saturation of the dedicated GPU pool serving Payfolio's reservation. Telemetry shows KV cache eviction rates spiking and longer queue retention for large-context requests. Kernel selection fallback observed on several nodes (likely spilling to slower kernels).
2) Impact: sustained increased latency; error surface primarily 5xx from timeouts rather than model corruption. Customer-facing effect: slowed checkout and degraded UX on heavy pages.

Immediate recommended actions (<= 60 minutes):
- Authorize emergency burst: provision 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs on Dedicated as burst for 3 hours (billing commit retroactive). This buys headroom while infra works the degradation.
- Apply routing policy change: divert 15% of Payfolio production QPS to verified hosted model variant in us-west-2. Hosted variant respects encryption at rest and TLS in transit; confirm E2E data handling with Payfolio (Dylan).
- Hotfix: bump prefix cache TTL for Payfolio's model endpoints to reduce KV thrash; infra to push within 20m.
- Monitoring: open a temporary dashboard with per-route token breakdown and KV hit/miss. Attach: reservation-report-20261121.csv and a short trace.

I'll be on the bridge. If exec approve burst, we should notify legal for an SLA exception/credit memo.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Success
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): reservation-report-20261121.csv, payfolio-mta-trace.txt
From: jonas_weber
To: vivek_kulkarni, rishi_malhotra
Cc: marissa_cole, dylan_brooks
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — approval request

Vivek / Rishi — we need quick authorization to proceed with the two cost levers Marissa outlined: emergency burst (4 GPUs, ~3 hours) and routing 15% to hosted fallback. Customer impact is material and this customer is in late-stage renewal (deal DL-90432). If we do nothing we risk a retention hit and an urgent exec escalation from Payfolio.

Ask: approve emergency burst and a provisional credit up to $X (finance to confirm), plus sign-off to route a subset of traffic to hosted for 4 hours. If approved, I'll notify Finance/Legal and confirm retroactive billing terms.

If we cannot approve burst, provide a clear fallback (reduce QPS via throttling or scheduled maintenance window) and Dylan please prep comms.

— Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success Ops
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <ops@payfolio.com>
To: dylan_brooks
Cc: payfolio-support@payfolio.com, procurement@payfolio.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — urgent

Dylan — thanks for the quick reaction. We can accept a hosted fallback for up to 20% of traffic for the next 4 hours as long as (a) no PII leaves the us-west-2 region and (b) logs/telemetry are not shared outside our SOC team. Confirm those two items and we will greenlight the diversion. Also need an ETA for when you expect KV hit ratio and 5xxs to normalize with the proposed actions.

— Alex
From: vivek_kulkarni
To: jonas_weber, marissa_cole, rishi_malhotra, dylan_brooks
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop on reserved pool (Payfolio) — exec decision and next steps

Approved: emergency burst (4 GPUs) and routing up to 20% of Payfolio traffic to the hosted fallback in us-west-2 for a maximum of 4 hours. Conditions:
- Ensure data residency: hosted fallback must be pinned to us-west-2 and logs must be scoped to Payfolio SOC. No cross-region replication.
- Finance: capture estimated burst spend and tie to Deal DL-90432 for later credit evaluation.
- Legal: prepare a short SLA exception note for Payfolio and a one-time credit proposal.

Operational next steps (owners):
- Infra (Rishi): provision burst + push prefix TTL hotfix now (target: 25m).
- CS (Marissa): confirm routed percentage and update Payfolio comms.
- Sales (Dylan): coordinate procurement side and confirm Payfolio consents on logs/data scope.
- Ops (Jonas): monitor the temporary dashboard and notify execs if metrics do not recover in 90 minutes.

I'll be looped in if we see persistent errors after the mitigation window. Good work triaging.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
